market_holds: ADS closed 2026-11-20 at $0.90 (Yahoo daily bars; the sealed baseline spot of $0.99 is from 18:09 UTC). That day was -15% and it is the first close below $1. The ADS is down about 68% from the $2.78 price of the August 2026 registered direct with Armistice and about 52% over 20 sessions, in a near-unbroken daily slide on tiny volume (about 27k ADS a day, so roughly $25k of turnover). Market cap is about $4.5M (4,978,216 ADS outstanding on 2026-09-24 per the F-1; Armistice holds 514,365 ADS = 9.99% capped, per its 13G of 2026-11-16, which implies about 5.15M ADS). Against that, cash was $13.1M at 30 June, a net $3.3M was raised in August, and the Kreos (BlackRock) loan was about $6.7M. There is no option chain and no consensus worth the name. The company's own guide is runway into 1H 2027, with a going-concern paragraph in the FY2025 audit. Already public before the print: the 2026-11-18 royalty sale ($5.6M for 80% of the APHEXDA royalty, of which $3.0M prepays Kreos, the $4M minimum-cash covenant is removed, and Chardan takes a $0.4M fee); the 2026-11-16 GLIX1 update (fourth cohort, results in 1H 2027); and the call date. The tape has already reacted to both: +2.7% on 295k ADS on 11-18, then -8% and -15%; -11.5% on the SNO day. Last three prints: FY25 on 2026-03-23 -12.5% on the day; Q1 around 2026-05-18/19 -6% then -6%; Q2 on 2026-08-31 +7.7%, confounded by the offering three days earlier. Typical size is about 6-12%.
view: A nano-cap biotech trading well below its cash, with a persistent seller and tax-loss season working on it. The Q3 release should hold little that is not already public. My cash estimate for 30 September is about $12M. The royalty deal plus the end of the covenant may let management stretch the runway from 1H 2027 into 2H 2027, but the market got that information on 11-18 and kept selling, so a runway line is mostly a restatement of a deal the tape has already digested. The things that could move it are unpredictable binaries of small expected size. Upside: a pancreatic Phase 2 interim (a 40% PFS-event look that the Q2 release said was expected in 2026) reported as passed, or a clearly longer runway headline. Downside: an ADS-ratio change or a reverse-split plan now that the ADS is under $1, stronger going-concern wording, or 'exploring strategic alternatives'. The flow on Monday morning is probably still Armistice and tax-loss sellers. Against that, a -15% close at a fresh low in a $4.5M name can snap back on almost nothing. I cannot separate these, so I see a near coin flip with a slight lean to continuation.

recommendation.reason: The financing and pipeline news that matters was released before the print (11-16 and 11-18), and the tape traded through both with continued selling. So the Q3 release is unlikely to reveal anything directional that the price lacks. The rest is overhang flow against oversold mean reversion in an illiquid ADS, which I cannot call to 65%.
recommendation.what_would_flip_it: A runway extension into 2028, or a reported pass of the pancreatic interim, would lean long. An ADS-ratio or reverse-split announcement, or strategic-alternatives language, would lean short.

self_critique: The ADS trades at about a third of gross cash, and the company may well headline an extended runway on Monday after removing the covenant. In a $4.5M float after a -15% capitulation day, even a modest buyer could lift it 10-20% by 13:00, so a long case on a mean-reversion pop is real. On the other side, a short case on continued Armistice and tax-loss selling is equally real. Neither clears 65%.
approach_notes: P4 helped: checking how the tape traded the 11-18 royalty news showed the financing was already digested rather than unpriced. On a nano-cap with no consensus and no options, P1-P3's consensus and preview machinery had little to work on, and the decision came down to flow, which the playbook barely covers.
